Subnautica: Below Zero feels like a mishmash of cut content from the original game taped together with a story that somehow manages to be too convoluted and too simple at the same time. Which is exactly what it is. While by no means a bad game, Below Zero really fails to live up to its predecessor, with environments and ecosystems that fail to blend together in the same way the original set of biomes did. It’s not terrible, but I can’t in good faith recommend buying and playing Sub Zero over replaying the original. It’s overall a downgrade from the original experience in most ways, and the Quality of Life changes I once praised the game for have since been ported over to the original, leaving me even less reason to revisit this sequel.

Not liking the direction of the story now after the change but I'll update this review after full release. For now I'd recommend you save your money until there's a sale or something.

Also I know the game is in early access but the story did a 180 on people. Now I feel like I spent money on a story that doesn't exist anymore.

Below Zero is good. The new creatures are beautiful, the environments are gorgeous, and visually it does have that Subnautica DNA (though not entirely)

But somehow... it just doesn't FEEL like Subnautica to me.

I can't even fully explain it. The original made me feel like I was genuinely stranded on this enormous alien ocean world, completely alone and discovering things I was never supposed to see. Below Zero feels smaller, more guided, more talkative and just... less mysterious.

The story also really wasn't my cup of tea. I know they wanted to make it more character-driven this time around, but personally I much preferred the lonely, environmental storytelling of the original.

Still a good game, still a beautiful alien ocean to explore, but compared to the first Subnautica it feels like something important got lost along the way.

6/10

Also, it was decided to leave the epic Cyclops submarine out of this game, which is a bit of a bummer (although the Seatruck performs very similarly, and is a fun vehicle to use).

Brilliant game. I haven't experienced everything that Below Zero has to offer but, so far, It did not disappoint. This series is still unmatched in terms of ambience and sound design. From pretty rainbow color pallets, to all the eerie shades of blues you can imagine, the impressiveness is superb. The wails and screeches of the creatures are top notch quality, which results in the occasional jump scare and spilled tea. The extra land exploration is also a nice addition. That said, the game does hold your hand quite a bit compared to the first one, but you still get a great sense of progression. Solid story so far, with interesting characters. That said, coming from the first Subnautica, I find it weird that my character developed the ability to retort. It's not that it's bad that your character speaks and expresses their opinions once in a while, it's just... weird.
Overall, I reckon its a great game, definitely worth the money, and a must buy on sale. I can't wait to finish the game and for the next installment of Subnautica!

Riley as a silent protagonist worked so well. He didn't need to tell you every time something happened like "That Reaper Leviathan sure looks dangerous! I better avoid it!" because the game relied on atmosphere and sound to tell you to better avoid it. The game isn't nearly as scary when you have two obnoxious constantly-talking protagonists stating the obvious all the time.

Please, PLEASE stick to a silent protagonist in the next installment, and use the money you save on VAs on better sound design of hostile creatures.

I went into it with an open mind and fresh out of the first entry in the Series. While I can’t say it’s a bad game, but something always felt off about it. While the game itself is generally mechanically the same as the original, every aspect of it somehow feels worse than the first entry - the story is all over the place and frankly very confusing and disjointed. It didn’t work well at all. Also, the world, while being smaller, felt vastly more empty. And finally, considering a lot of new additions felt very janky and unpolished, it is safe to assume that the game was very undercooked and not well thought through. Had it had more polish and refine, and released as an expansion instead of a separate entry, it would work as a great addition to an already amazing Subnautica. But as a separate entry, it doesn’t feel as great.

To sum up - I really wanted to like it, and while there are some interesting and enjoyable elements, I did not enjoy the game as a whole.

Unfortunately, it's nowhere as good as the original. It has some marginal improvements, but the narrative just doesn't mesh at all with the unguided open-world exploration, and it doesn't try to replicate the vibe of desperate solitude. The overland stuff is also just not well-suited to this game engine, which feels super smooth underwater but super janky on land. If you're thinking of playing this before Subnautica, definitely get the original instead: if you're thinking of it AFTER Subnautica, just be aware that it's trying to do something different narratively, not more of the same.

Content - The game is not yet complete but I already got my money's worth out of it. I have progressed the story as far as possible right now, and am looking forward to see its conclusion when the game comes out of early access. Compared to the original Subnautica (which you don't have to know) some content has been replaced (most notably vehicles) while other content (like base parts) has been added.

Design - Some of the new biomes outshine everything I have seen in Subnautica, while others are... let's just say I travel through them but I don't go there to enjoy the view. The game world now includes a larger land area which can be confusing at times because of limited visibility (a weather system has been added to the game, including fog.)

Stability - Having played for about 190 hours I did not experience any game-breaking bugs but I fully acknowlegde that others have had different experiences. Also, I have carried over experiences and behaviours from the original Subnautica which may have helped me avoid issues. There are still new (or repeated) bug reports on the forum but the focus seems to shift from reporting bugs to content discussions, which seems to indicate that bugs aren't as frequent as they used to be.

Lots of time and effort has gone into this, as of the time of this review I'd give it another two years in the oven, especially since the story is getting completely reworked. Participate in the feedback and beta program(as buggy as it is) else you might not see the scale of their task at hand.

This game didn't feel like it's predecessor. Some of the resources you've been conditioned in the first game to locate based on biomes and such got flipped over it's head for a start, on top of that the rarer resources come so late in game they become useless.

The map itself felt like they just wrote a story first then created the checkpoints around the center and became an oversized fetch quest. The game felt more like a chore and I was becoming less and less interested in exploring and more inclined to just finish this game and get it over with.

The nail in the coffin are the characters and story writing, it seems like they had a diversity checklist this time around:
- diverse female MC making unfunny remarks every 5 minutes
- same sex relationship that doesn't even go anywhere story wise
- incompetent men

And this is a shame because Maida makes an appearance and she is as badass as before and they don't do much with it.

The new building modules and vehicles were fun but again the game just turns into such a bad fetch quest you hardly make any use for a base.

There were some spectacular elements in the game but not even half as many as in the first.

I have played Subnautica Below Zero for 34 hours already, but I am starting to feel, that I will not finish this game. Here are my reasons:

Pro:
The graphic is realy good
The sound is good
The story is not so good as in Subnautica, but still feels OK

Con:
After playing first Subnautica for 4 times already, the world in Below Zero feels really empty - fewer resources, not much flora/fauna, huge areas without anything at all

The empty feeling about the world is the reason why I am dissapointed with the game. If you really want to play Subnautica, play the first game. It has so much more of everything than Below Zero.

Frustration simulator. In the early game upgrade fragments are everywhere. In the mid and late game most things can only be found one way. The game can't decide if it wants to be open ended or not which contributes to frustration. Some blueprints are open ended and can be discovered various ways. Other cannot. It's silly that I'm unlocking blueprints for cool stuff when my next task is to make a 1 hour trip to end the game.

The first game was good about giving the player clear directions and technology for finding things. This game departs from that and uses clues and hints on some critical elements. It's frustrating because the player is trained by the game to play and progress a certain way, then the means become finding and listening to the right verbal/visual clues, brute force, or looking up the missing things on the internet.

The first 5-10 hours of this game is solid. The rest feels unfinished and unpolished.

This is not the Subnautica sequel that you have been looking for.
They have removed most of the things from the game that made the original fun.
This game feels like a poorly written DLC that got pawned off as a full size game.

Intrigue driven story - Removed
Ocean Exploration - Removed
Submarine Exploration - Removed

This game takes place basically in a small lake, hardly living up to it's name.
Map size is roughly 1/4 the size of it's predecessor. The game seems to lack coherent vision, as if the map was designed first, and a story written to the constraints as an after thought.

As a stand alone game, this isn't bad, but not worth full price.
If you liked the Original, don't walk into this one expecting the same feel.

Equal parts terrifying and relaxing! If you enjoy survival games with a heavy emphasis on exploration, you'll be addicted to this. The intelligent and aesthetic design of alien life and the varying environments are sure to keep you enthralled. Very easy to navigate in-game mechanics and controls. The hints throughout the game are very useful, yet optional. In conclusion... GET IT!!!
What made the original so good was the story. This game is an improvement in all aspects except that which mattered most. It is still a enjoyable game with a similar atmosphere to the first game.
